descriptionChirho: The proper noun Ἰωάνης (Iōannēs) referring to various New Testament figures named John (the Baptist, the Apostle, John Mark, etc.). The two clusters represent the same name across different grammatical cases: nominative/accusative (130x) vs dative/genitive with prepositions (5x). Multilingual evidence is uniform: Spanish 'Iōánnēs,' Hindi 'यूहन्ना/योहान्नान,' Arabic 'يوحنّا,' Korean '요한,' Swahili 'Yohana.' Case-form variation (e.g., 'to-Iōannēs' vs 'Iōannēs') does not constitute a distinct lexicographic sense.
